title: Fitting ideals of a finite module: independence of generators and base change
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and let $k\ge0$ be an integer. For an $R$-linear surjection $\pi:R^{\oplus n}\to M$ with kernel $K\subset R^{\oplus n}$, let $I_k(\pi)\subset R$ be the ideal generated by the $(n-k)\times(n-k)$ minors of all $(n-k)\times n$ matrices [def-weil-matrix] whose rows are elements of $K$, with $I_k(\pi)=R$ when $n\le k$. Then: (1) $I_k(\pi)=I_k(\pi')$ for any two $R$-linear surjections $\pi:R^{\oplus n}\to M$ and $\pi':R^{\oplus n'}\to M$; (2) for every ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to R'$, the surjection $\pi\otimes_RR':R'^{\oplus n}\to M\otimes_RR'$ satisfies $I_k(\pi\otimes_RR')=\varphi(I_k(\pi))R'$. In particular, for $g\in R$ the ideal $I_k$ of the $R_g$-module $M_g$ is $I_k(\pi)R_g$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal) for (1), including the description by minors of matrices with rows in the kernel given at the start of its proof; Lemma Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics) part (3) for (2); used in Divisors Section Tag 0C3C (section-fitting-ideals) to glue the Fitting ideal sheaves

proof.text: For $K=\ker\pi$, the defining ideal $I_k(\pi)$ is exactly $D_k(K;n)$ of [lem-trf-row-minor-ideal-stable-invariance]. Its clauses (1)-(3) give the finite-row description, invariance upon adjoining any number of zero generators, and invariance under invertible free coordinates, including $n\le k$.

For $\pi:F=R^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow M$ and $\pi\prime:G=R^{\oplus m}\twoheadrightarrow M$, apply [lem-trf-free-surjections-common-stabilization] to obtain the commuting isomorphism $U:F\oplus G\to G\oplus F$ identifying $\ker\pi\oplus G$ with $\ker\pi\prime\oplus F$. Both ambient modules have rank $n+m$. By [lem-trf-row-minor-ideal-stable-invariance](3) their row-minor ideals agree; by its clause (2) these ideals are respectively $I_k(\pi)$ and $I_k(\pi\prime)$. This proves (1).

For $\varphi:R\to R\prime$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] to $K\hookrightarrow R^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\pi}M\to0$, tensoring with $R\prime$. Thus $\pi\otimes1$ is surjective and its kernel is the image of $K\otimes_R R\prime$, without any injectivity claim. The coordinate isomorphism in [lem-trf-row-minor-ideal-scalar-extension] identifies this image with $K_{R\prime}$. If $n>k$, use its ideal equality at $r=n-k$ to get $I_k(\pi\otimes1)=\varphi(I_k(\pi))R\prime$. If $n\le k$, both ideals are the unit ideal. This proves (2).

Take $R\prime=R_g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor], the natural isomorphism $M\otimes_RR_g\to M_g$, $m\otimes(a/g^e)\mapsto am/g^e$, identifies $\pi\otimes1$ with $\pi_g$. The base-change equality just proved gives $I_k(\pi_g)=I_k(\pi)R_g$, and (1) makes this the ideal of the localized module independently of its presentation.

proof_origin.place: 07Z8 proof (kernel rows, zero stabilization, invertible coordinate change), and 07ZA(3) proof (tensor right exactness); the Schanuel comparison is expanded by explicit invertible shears.

lean.statement: theorem presentationFittingIdeal_independence_baseChange {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (k : ℕ) {n : ℕ} (π : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] M) (hπ : Function.Surjective π) : (∀ (n' : ℕ) (π' : (Fin n' → R) →ₗ[R] M), Function.Surjective π' → π.presentationFittingIdeal k = π'.presentationFittingIdeal k) ∧ (∀ (A : Type w) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A], Function.Surjective (π.baseChangePresentation A) ∧ (π.baseChangePresentation A).presentationFittingIdeal k = Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) (π.presentationFittingIdeal k)) ∧ (∀ g : R, Function.Surjective (π.localizePresentationAway g) ∧ (π.localizePresentationAway g).presentationFittingIdeal k = Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Localization.Away g)) (π.presentationFittingIdeal k))
lean.note: The three helper definitions give the ideal and the canonical base-changed/localized presentations introduced in this node, with real data. All ring maps are represented by arbitrary Algebra R A instances; algebraMap is the chosen ring map. The tensor factor order follows the recorded module-base-change dependency.
